hero.title: Provider & Fee Benchmarking
hero.subtitle: Independent fee benchmarking that helps demonstrate fee reasonableness and strengthen your fiduciary process.

blocks.text: One of the most important responsibilities under ERISA is ensuring your retirement plan fees remain reasonable for the services your participants receive. That responsibility doesn't end once your plan is established. Providers change, pricing evolves, and growing plans often qualify for better fee structures than they received years ago.

PointOak Retirement Advisors provides independent 401(k) fee benchmarking that evaluates every layer of plan expenses—not just recordkeeping fees. Our process compares your actual retirement plan against current market data to help your committee understand total plan costs, identify opportunities for improvement, and document a prudent fiduciary review process.

body.text: ERISA requires fiduciaries to determine whether plan fees remain reasonable relative to the services provided. Independent benchmarking creates the documentation your committee needs to support that determination.

Retirement plan expenses often extend well beyond a single recordkeeping fee. We evaluate investment expenses, administrative fees, revenue sharing, advisory compensation, and indirect costs to provide a complete picture of your plan.

Knowing current market pricing gives your committee leverage during provider renewal discussions. Benchmarking often creates opportunities to negotiate improved pricing or enhanced services without changing providers.

Every dollar spent unnecessarily on plan expenses is a dollar that no longer compounds for participants. Identifying excessive costs helps improve long-term retirement outcomes without changing participant behavior.
Fee benchmarking isn't simply about reducing costs—it's about documenting a prudent, repeatable process that demonstrates ongoing fiduciary oversight.

blocks.text: Effective fee benchmarking evaluates far more than a single invoice or expense ratio.

PointOak reviews recordkeeping fees, investment management expenses, revenue-sharing arrangements, participant-paid charges, advisory compensation, administrative costs, and indirect compensation using your actual retirement plan data. Those findings are then compared against similarly sized retirement plans and current marketplace pricing.

blocks.lead: Independent fee benchmarking is especially valuable when:
items: Your plan has not been benchmarked in the past two to three years.
Your provider contract is approaching renewal.
Committee members are questioning whether current fees remain reasonable.
Your organization has experienced significant growth.
Your retirement plan has increased substantially in assets or participants.
You're preparing for a Department of Labor review or fiduciary audit.
You cannot clearly identify every fee participants are paying.

blocks.text: Recently benchmarked plans with stable pricing may only require periodic monitoring, but most growing retirement plans benefit from regular independent fee reviews.

sections.title: Annual Fee Review and Periodic Full Benchmarking

blocks.text: PointOak generally conducts a full plan and provider benchmark every three to five years, or sooner when circumstances warrant. In years when we are not conducting a full benchmark, we perform a fee benchmark and work with the provider to reprice the plan annually. The three-to-five-year interval is PointOak's practice, not a DOL or ERISA requirement.

items.q: What fees should be included in a 401(k) fee benchmark?

a.text: A complete fee benchmark evaluates every layer of plan expenses.

This includes recordkeeping fees, investment management fees, expense ratios, advisory compensation, administrative costs, participant-paid charges, revenue-sharing arrangements, and other indirect compensation. Looking at only one fee category rarely provides an accurate picture of total plan costs.

items.q: What is fee reasonableness under ERISA?

a.text: ERISA requires fiduciaries to evaluate whether retirement plan fees are reasonable for the services being provided.

Reasonable does not necessarily mean lowest. Committees should consider pricing alongside service quality, participant support, compliance resources, technology, investment flexibility, and overall value when evaluating providers.

items.q: Does benchmarking mean we should change providers?

a.text: Many benchmarking engagements confirm that an existing provider continues to offer competitive pricing and appropriate service. Others identify opportunities to renegotiate fees without changing providers. Only when significant differences exist does a competitive provider search typically become the recommended next step.

items.q: How do you identify hidden retirement plan fees?

a.text: Hidden costs often appear as indirect compensation rather than clearly disclosed invoices.

PointOak reviews revenue-sharing arrangements, asset-based charges, fund expenses, administrative costs, transaction fees, and other indirect compensation to provide a complete picture of your retirement plan's cost structure.

items.q: Can fee benchmarking lower participant costs?

a.text: Independent benchmarking frequently identifies opportunities to reduce recordkeeping fees, improve investment share classes, eliminate unnecessary expenses, or renegotiate provider contracts. Even relatively small cost reductions can produce meaningful long-term savings for participants through compound growth.

items.q: What's the difference between fee benchmarking and a retirement plan RFP?

a.text: Fee benchmarking evaluates your current provider's pricing against the marketplace.

A retirement plan RFP is a competitive bidding process used when benchmarking suggests your committee should formally evaluate alternative providers. Benchmarking helps determine whether an RFP is necessary.
